需要讓網友在 BIOS 核顯開啟、故障出現時，補發：

  - Magpie 目錄下的 ReShade.log
  - 整個 DLSS5-AMD\logs 文件夾
  - 畫面上具體顯示的錯誤文字
[magpie.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32527178/magpie.zip) 已按照要求提取日志。只有这两个日志无其他的，也不显示错误
黄色字体显示如图，DL5S5-AMD: INIT FAILED - SEE DLSS5-A10\L0GS

## AMD iGPU + RX 9070 XT: HIP device is correctly matched by LUID, but first network launch fails with `hipErrorInvalidHandle (400)`

### Environment

- AMD iGPU enabled
- AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
- Magpie + `dlss5-amd.addon64`
- HIP runtime: `70260201`
- HIP network architecture: `gfx1201`

The same setup works differently when only the discrete GPU is present / the iGPU is disabled.

### Symptom

The add-on successfully selects the RX 9070 XT through D3D12/HIP LUID matching:

```text
device=AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT
arch=gfx1201
match=luid
runtime=70260201
```

`native-hip.txt` also shows:

```text
hip_device=1
```

So adapter selection itself appears to be correct.

Network initialization succeeds and reaches `ready`, but the first actual render fails:

```text
event=render_begin detail=seed=0 temporal path armed (history from previous processed frame)
event=render_failed detail=c32_wave1_prefix_b8d: hipErrorInvalidHandle (400)
```

The session is then reset and the exact same failure repeats.

### Suspected cross-thread HIP device binding issue

Current `main` correctly finds the HIP device corresponding to the D3D12 adapter and sets:

```cpp
options.device = unsigned(chosen);
hip_device = chosen;
probe.hipSetDevice(chosen);
```

`Network` also calls `hipSetDevice(opt.device)` during construction.

However initialization happens on the background initialization thread, while the later network enqueue/render happens from another host thread.

`D3D12Bridge::Enqueue()` currently calls HIP APIs and `network->Enqueue()` without first restoring:

```cpp
hipSetDevice(hip_device)
```

HIP documents the current/default device as thread-local state.

I am not claiming this is definitively the root cause because the network uses an explicit HIP stream, but the combination is suspicious:

```text
HIP device 1 selected correctly
+ initialization succeeds
+ module/function creation succeeds
+ first actual module kernel launch
= hipErrorInvalidHandle (400)
```

This may be worth testing by explicitly rebinding the selected device at HIP entry points, starting with `D3D12Bridge::Enqueue()`:

```cpp
auto& api = network->Runtime();
api.Check(api.hipSetDevice(hip_device), "select HIP device for enqueue");
```

before the semaphore wait / `network->Enqueue()` calls.

It may also be useful to log `hipGetDevice()` from both the initialization thread and the render/enqueue thread to verify whether they differ (`1` vs `0`) on an iGPU + dGPU machine.

### Logs available

[native-hip.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33022042/native-hip.txt)
[native-hip-device.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33022043/native-hip-device.txt)
[native-game-oneshot.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33022044/native-game-oneshot.txt)

The important parts are that LUID matching already selects the RX 9070 XT successfully, while the first `c32_wave1_prefix_b8d` launch consistently returns `hipErrorInvalidHandle (400)`.

Tested this on one machine (AMD iGPU enabled + RX 9070 XT, Magpie, unchanged
flags, unchanged HIP modules). Three add-ons, only `dlss5-amd.addon64` swapped,
Magpie fully closed between rounds:

```
A  0.40 shipped add-on                 c511e148   render_failed x9   400
B  current main, cross-compiled        42f1de34   render_failed x9   400
C  current main + rebind in Enqueue    3864b54c   render_failed 0    render_complete
```

A and B fail with the same signature at the same kernel
(`c32_wave1_prefix_b8d: hipErrorInvalidHandle (400)`), so current main does not
fix this on its own. C reports zero `hipErrorInvalidHandle` in every log
(`native-game-oneshot`, `native-hip`, `native-hip-device`,
`native-submission-order`, `ReShade.log`) and keeps running — 600+ frames at
~15.0 ms/frame.

All three select the same device (`match=luid`, `hip_device=1`, `gfx1201`) and
log byte-identical runtime options (42 fields), and B logs the main-only
`predict_active` / `skin_active` lines that 0.40 does not have — so this is a
like-for-like comparison, not three different configurations.

Patch, build command and the full per-round run procedure: #15

Still open: no thread id was logged, so whether initialization and enqueue
actually run on different host threads is not proven. The patch only has to
hold the selected device across the enqueue path, which the A/B/C above shows
it does.
